decision: Generate Rust model from TypeScript declarations and committed per-type field orders
why: Fields missing from corpus must not rely on hand transcription

decision: Compare model JSON as UTF-8 blobs, Maps as entries and bytes as base64 markers
why: JSON alone hides Maps; a JSON header would reprint the model before comparison

decision: Use portable Node 22.23.5; discard Node24-started check
why: Main reports measured host-dependent inflater behavior and now enforces Node22

decision: Parse all tracked documents and existing property synthetic bodies
why: Exercise full model, not just individual property readers
result: 183 corpus and 220 built results; 4 refusals recorded

decision: Keep the first model comparison as it came out, before any fix
why: The equality rate before fixing is the measure of the port
result: 9,834 checks: 2,940 equal (29.9%), 6,894 differ, 5,579 of them by key order only

decision: Take the key order of a type from parser results only; schema-built values never vote
why: Review found 32 types marked input by built values that set keys in an order no parser path takes
result: 7 input types, 61 fixed by parser evidence, 81 in declaration order without evidence

decision: Add values the model must refuse, one broken thing each
why: A strict reader that is never shown an invalid value is not checked to be strict
result: 1,880 of 1,880 refused on the first run

decision: Refuse an enum written as an object and a Record<number> key that is no number; add a value of every other JSON kind per field
why: Review: serde's derived enum reader takes {"left":null}; the first run of the wider set found NumberingDef.startOverrides accepting a non-number key
result: 13,246 values: 13,245 refused on the first run, 13,246 after the fix

decision: Commit the first runs gzipped, with the SHA-256 of each file as written
why: 16 MB of digests; gzip -9 -n keeps the bytes

decision: Generate EffectivePPr and EffectiveRPr from resolve-props.ts instead of holding them opaque; do not use the structs of resolve.rs as the model fields
why: resolve.rs reads them leniently for its own callers and nests reader-local types the model already has; its field orders are the check
result: 11 types added; every order equals resolve.rs; ParaBorderLine corrected to color, szPt, none, spacePt

decision: Declare the 7 path-ordered types with jscompat::js_object! and Slot; drop the model's key_order
why: One mechanism for key order across the crates, the one the readers already build with
result: first run after the change: 23,816 checks, 0 differences
